loop.top3_why: Candidate B uses a trimmed‑mean over the full pool of 9 best‑ranked models, providing robustness against a few outlier models while still leveraging the full diversity of the pool. The trimmed‑mean also mitigates the risk of correlated errors among models, which is a concern noted in the diagnosis. The overall validation score is the best among the three candidates and the gap to the leader is zero, showing it is the top performer.
loop.top3_why_not: Candidate A (mean pool1) shows a positive error in one window, suggesting it is more sensitive to a single poorly performing model. Candidate C (mean pool3) has a slightly positive error in one window and a higher overall score, indicating less stability. Both are less robust than the trimmed‑mean approach of B, especially given the moderate ranking stability (Kendall tau 0.4) and the risk of correlated errors highlighted in the diagnosis.
